messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
When you throw a ball straight upward, it experiences a constant downward acceleration due to gravity—about \(9.8 \text{ m/s}^2\) on Earth.  
That means the ball’s acceleration is **\(a = -9.8 \text{ m/s}^2\)** (negative because it points opposite to the upward direction).  

This value does not depend on the initial speed; whether you launch it at 5 m/s or 20 m/s, the acceleration remains the same (ignoring air resistance).
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" They want the acceleration. But acceleration due to gravity is constant ~9.8 m/s^2 downward. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2 (downwards). We can mention that acceleration is independent of initial velocity. Provide explanation. No function call needed.
